A pucca house, a separate gate and a 'good address' are long-horizon status projects.
Clothing signals occasion, community and respectability; premium is read through fabric and brand, not just price.
Purchase decisions are often family and community decisions; visible consumption invites judgement.
House, gold and vehicle purchases may be timed to auspicious dates; rational to the household even when it looks inefficient.
Occupation and credit networks are still community-linked in many towns; trust travels through known networks.
Households optimise for repairability, local spare parts and informal service, not just warranty terms.
One visible owner in the same street or apartment block outweighs a national ad for high-involvement purchases.

regions.name: North
regions.summary: Agrarian hinterland, dense towns, strong status competition and family-mediated purchases.
regions.consumption: Festival and wedding spending are highly visible; gold, vehicles and electronics carry family prestige. Sachets and EMI bridge irregular cash flows.
regions.gender: Women's mobility and paid work vary sharply by community and state; purdah, safety and family permission still shape access.
regions.status: Address, vehicle, phone and children's English-medium schooling are the core status markers.
regions.constraints: Seasonal income, groundwater stress, air pollution, weak last-mile service in small towns.
regions.culture: Hindi belt sociality, caste networks, temple towns, migration to Delhi/NCR and Punjab-to-abroad links.

regions.name: South
regions.summary: Higher urbanisation, stronger human development, language pride and a dense tier-2 town network.
regions.consumption: Education, healthcare and durable goods are prioritised; filter coffee, rice, gold and silk carry cultural weight. Premium adoption travels through tier-2 towns faster than in the north.
regions.gender: Kerala and Tamil Nadu show comparatively better female literacy and mobility, but paid work and safety still vary.
regions.status: Education, house, car and children's professional careers; 'good family' matters more than display in some communities.
regions.constraints: Water stress, congestion, high land prices, dependence on inter-state migrant labour.
regions.culture: Temple festivals, classical arts, film and language politics; Bengaluru and Hyderabad are tech-migration cities.

regions.name: West
regions.summary: Trade-led, entrepreneurial, highly urban and deeply connected to global commodity and migration flows.
regions.consumption: Gujarat's business networks and Maharashtra's metro aspiration create a wide spread: from diamond workers to luxury South Mumbai. Credit and dealer relationships are central.
regions.gender: Female work participation varies; Goa and urban Maharashtra are more liberal, while conservative pockets persist.
regions.status: Business scale, property, gold and vehicles; community reputation is a credit asset.
regions.constraints: Housing cost, water, congestion, migrant labour dependence, cyclical commodity exposure.
regions.culture: Garba, Ganesh Chaturthi, Diwali, business-family networks, Bollywood and a strong cooperative tradition.

regions.name: East
regions.summary: Young, rural-heavy and migration-linked, with strong cultural identity and uneven industrialisation.
regions.consumption: Price sensitivity is high; sachets, second-hand goods and local repair markets matter. Festivals like Durga Puja and Chhath drive concentrated spending.
regions.gender: Women's work is rising in some pockets but mobility remains constrained; migration of men reshapes households.
regions.status: Education, government jobs, land and house; Kolkata's cultural capital carries regional prestige.
regions.constraints: Floods, weak industrial base, transport costs, limited formal credit, out-migration.
regions.culture: Bengali, Odia, Assamese and tribal identities; tea, fish, rice and strong literary/film traditions.

regions.name: Central
regions.summary: Agrarian and forest-dependent, with large tribal populations and significant poverty concentration.
regions.consumption: Food and fuel dominate budgets; durable purchases are deferred and often financed through informal credit or gold.
regions.gender: Early marriage and low female mobility persist in many districts; SHG networks are a countervailing force.
regions.status: Land, house, motorcycle and children's education; display is moderated by community norms.
regions.constraints: Rainfed agriculture, forest rights, poor connectivity, health and education gaps.
regions.culture: Tribal festivals, folk music, pilgrimage towns and Hindi-language media.

regions.name: Northeast
regions.summary: Distinct ethnic and linguistic identities, high literacy in places, and severe logistics constraints.
regions.consumption: Small markets, high landed costs and strong community networks. Christianity, tribal customs and local languages shape trust.
regions.gender: Matrilineal pockets (Khasi, Garo) contrast with patrilineal communities; women's market presence is visible.
regions.status: Community standing, education and government employment; outside brands must earn local legitimacy.
regions.constraints: Terrain, inner-line permits, small market size, poor road/air connectivity, limited service networks.
regions.culture: Hornbill, Bihu, Sangai and tribal festivals; music, football and local fashion are strong identity markers.

norms.detail: Big-ticket decisions are negotiated with parents, spouses and sometimes elders; a lone 'consumer' is the exception.
norms.effect: Raises the bar for high-involvement categories; family demos and guarantor-friendly finance help.

norms.detail: One visible owner in the same street, block or WhatsApp group is stronger evidence than a national ad.
norms.effect: Accelerates adoption after first local owner; also accelerates rejection after a visible failure.

norms.detail: The local dealer is judged on service, resale and whether they will still be there next year.
norms.effect: Service density and dealer reputation are adoption infrastructure.

norms.detail: Visible consumption is read as character; families avoid shame and envy as much as they seek prestige.
norms.effect: Can suppress show-off categories and boost 'safe' premium signals (education, gold, house).

norms.detail: Households optimise for repairability, local spare parts and informal service over official warranty.
norms.effect: Favours modular, repairable products; punishes sealed, service-dependent designs.

norms.detail: A scheme or subsidy can legitimise a category, but paperwork and last-mile delivery decide take-up.
norms.effect: Policy scenarios should model friction, not just price cuts.

norms.detail: Purchases may be timed to festivals, muhurat or harvest cash; demand is lumpy and socially coordinated.
norms.effect: Festival scenarios should lift both demand and price tolerance, then decay.

norms.detail: Gold is savings, marriage insurance and status; it competes with financial products for the same rupee.
norms.effect: Financial products must beat gold on trust and liquidity, not only returns.

norms.detail: Families cut current consumption for English-medium schooling, coaching and college.
norms.effect: Education categories have unusual price tolerance and long decision cycles.

norms.detail: Local-language creative signals respect; English-only creative signals distance.
norms.effect: Localisation is not translation; idiom and reference matter.

norms.detail: Fairness and colour bias shape beauty, matrimony and self-presentation.
norms.effect: Model as a bias with ethical caveats; do not present it as a recommendation.

norms.detail: Mobility, evening use and solo travel are negotiated against family honour and safety.
norms.effect: Products that reduce safety friction (home delivery, verified drivers, women-only services) travel faster.

norms.detail: A forward from a trusted contact can outweigh an official correction.
norms.effect: Fact-checking must travel through the same network; mass media alone does not correct it.

norms.detail: In small communities, visible excess can invite envy; understatement is sometimes safer.
norms.effect: Premium brands need a 'quiet' variant and a local legitimacy story.

norms.detail: The distance to a service centre is priced into the purchase, especially for vehicles and durables.
norms.effect: Service guarantees matter more than feature lists outside metros.

norms.detail: Migrant earnings support a village household; spending is negotiated across two locations.
norms.effect: Remittance cycles create seasonal demand and conservative risk appetite.
